# Jubilees Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abram in Canaan and Egypt; Tithe to Melchizedek; War of Kings

---

**13:1** He moved from there and went southward, coming to Hebron — which had just been built at that time — and he lived there two years. Then he went further south to Bealoth, but there was a famine in the land.

**13:2** Abram went into Egypt in the third year of the week, and he lived in Egypt five years before his wife was taken from him.

**13:3** At that time Tanis in Egypt had just been built — seven years after Hebron.

**13:4** When Pharaoh took Sarai, Abram's wife, the LORD afflicted Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues on account of Sarai.

**13:5** Abram became very wealthy in possessions — silver and gold, cattle, donkeys, horses, camels, male and female servants, and great riches.

**13:6** Lot, who had traveled with Abram, also had possessions of his own — flocks, oxen, and donkeys.

**13:7** Abram and his wife returned from Egypt to the place where he had first pitched his tent, between Bethel and Ai.

**13:8** They parted from there: Lot went down to the valley, and Abram remained in the hill country.

**13:9** Lot settled in Sodom, and the people of Sodom were exceedingly wicked.

**13:10** Abram was grieved in his heart that his nephew had separated from him, for he had no children.

**13:11** In the year when Lot was taken captive — in the fourth year of that week, after Lot had separated from him — the LORD said to Abram: "Lift up your eyes from the place where you are dwelling, and look northward and southward, and westward and eastward."

**13:12** "For all the land that you see, I will give to you and to your descendants forever, and I will make your descendants like the sand of the sea; though a person can count the sand of the sea, yet your descendants shall not be numbered."

**13:13** "Rise up, walk through the land in all its length and breadth and see it, for to your descendants I will give it."

**13:14** Abram went to Hebron and settled there.

**13:15** In the thirteenth year of the third week of this jubilee, four kings made war with five kings; the five kings were routed before them, and Lot was taken captive along with all the possessions of Sodom.

**13:16** One who had escaped came and told Abram that his nephew Lot had been taken captive.

**13:17** Abram armed his household servants — three hundred and eighteen — and pursued the kings.

**13:18** He attacked them by night, pursued them to Dan, and struck them down. He recovered all the plunder and his nephew Lot along with all the goods.

**13:19** The king of Sodom came and bowed before him, saying: "Our lord Abram, give us the people you have rescued; take the plunder for yourself."

**13:20** Abram said to the king of Sodom: "I raise my hand to the LORD God Most High, who made heaven and earth, that I will take nothing belonging to you — not a thread, not a sandal strap — lest you say, 'I made Abram rich.'"

**13:21** "Only what my young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who came with me — Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre — let those take their portion."

**13:22** Abram gave a tithe of all the chief of the spoils to Melchizedek, and Melchizedek ate and drank.

**13:23** Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High, and he blessed Abram, saying: "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Lord of heaven and earth."

**13:24** "And blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand."

**13:25** And Abram gave him a tenth of all his goods.

**13:26** In this jubilee Abram lived in the land of Canaan for five weeks of years. In the sixth week, in the second year thereof, Abram took Hagar as a wife.

**13:27** Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian — her maidservant — and gave her to Abram her husband as a wife.

**13:28** Hagar bore Abram a son, and he named him Ishmael, in the fifth year of the sixth week.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS throughout. "God Most High" = El Elyon preserved consistently. Melchizedek as king of Salem and priest of God Most High (v.23) is rendered in full. "Five weeks of years" (v.26) retained as Jubilees calendrical expression.*
